claim: TRPV2 channel is a member of the temperature-sensing thermoTRPV family
source: The Transient Receptor Potential Vanilloid 2 (TRPV2) channel is a member of the temperature-sensing thermoTRPV family.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental support in this manuscript

claim: Crystallographic studies of ligand-dependent TRPV2 gating have shown that the TRPV2 channel adopts two-fold symmetric arrangements during the gating cycle
source: Interestingly, crystallographic studies of ligand-dependent TRPV2 gating have shown that the TRPV2 channel adopts two-fold symmetric arrangements during the gating cycle.
evidence: This refers to previous crystallographic studies, citing prior research findings

claim: RTx induces two-fold symmetric conformations of TRPV2 in both nanodiscs and amphipol environments
source: We show that RTx induces two-fold symmetric conformations of TRPV2 in both environments.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the cryo-EM structures presented in the manuscript

claim: The two-fold symmetry is more pronounced in the native-like lipid environment of the nanodiscs
source: However, the two-fold symmetry is more pronounced in the native-like lipid environment of the nanodiscs.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of the structures obtained in different environments

claim: TRPV channels play important roles in numerous physiological processes
source: Transient Receptor Potential V (TRPV) channels are part of the larger TRP channel family which plays important roles in numerous physiological processes (Clapham et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Clapham et al., 2001

claim: TRPV1-TRPV4 possess an intrinsic capability to sense heat
source: A subset of TRPV channels, including subtypes TRPV1-TRPV4, possess an intrinsic capability to sense heat and are therefore referred to as thermoTRPV channels (Cao et al., 2013a; Liu and Qin, 2016; Smith et al., 2002; Chung et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations

claim: TRPV1-TRPV4 are non-selective cation channels
source: TRPV1-TRPV4 are non-selective cation channels which play important physiological roles in sensing noxious heat (Bölcskei et al., 2010; Julius, 2013; Marwaha et al., 2016; Mitchell et al., 2014), maintaining cardiac structure (Katanosaka et al., 2014) and maintaining skin (Eytan et al., 2014; Imura et al., 2009; Kim et al., 2016), hair (Asakawa et al., 2006; Imura et al., 2007; Xiao et al., 2008) and bone physiology (Masuyama et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations

claim: TRPV1 and TRPV2 are permeable to large organic cations
source: A distinctive feature of TRPV1 and TRPV2 is their permeability to large organic cations (Chung et al., 2008), such as the cationic dye YO-PRO-1 and the sodium channel blocker QX-314.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chung et al., 2008

claim: TRPV1 and TRPV2 have been proposed as conduits for delivering small molecules to intracellular targets
source: This feature has led to proposals to utilize these channels as conduits for delivering small molecules to intracellular targets (Puopolo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Puopolo et al., 2013

claim: Non-conducting structures of TRPV1 and TRPV2 possess two restrictions: one at the selectivity filter and one at the intracellular mouth of the pore
source: The non-conducting structures of TRPV1 and TRPV2 possess two restrictions, one at the selectivity filter (SF) and second one at the intracellular mouth of the pore (termed the common gate) (Liao et al., 2013; Zubcevic et al., 2016; Huynh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations

claim: Both restrictions must open widely to accommodate the passage of large organic cations
source: Both restrictions must open widely to accommodate the passage of large organic cations.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the size of large organic cations and the structure of the channel

claim: Binding of RTx leads to a two-fold symmetric opening at the selectivity filter that is wide enough to permeate YO-PRO-1
source: This study led to the revelation that the binding of RTx leads to a two-fold symmetric (C2) opening at the selectivity filter that is wide enough to permeate YO-PRO-1.
evidence: This refers to findings from a previous crystallographic study by the authors

claim: Four structures of the TRPV2/RTx complex were determined: one in nanodiscs at 3.8 Å resolution and three in amphipol at 2.9 Å, 3.3 Å and 4.2 Å resolution
source: We present four structures of the TRPV2/RTx complex, one obtained in nanodiscs (TRPV2RTx-ND) and three in amphipol (TRPV2RTx-APOL 1-3) determined to 3.8 Å, 2.9 Å, 3.3 Å and 4.2 Å resolution, respectively (Table 1, Figure 1).
evidence: This is directly supported by the experimental data presented in Table 1 and Figure 1

claim: The extent of C2 symmetry depends on the environment in which the channel is reconstituted
source: Our data shows that binding of RTx induces C2 symmetric conformations in TRPV2, but the extent of C2 symmetry depends on the environment in which the channel is reconstituted.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of structures obtained in different environments

claim: C2 symmetry is particularly pronounced in the dataset collected from nanodisc-reconstituted TRPV2
source: C2 symmetry is particularly pronounced in the dataset collected from nanodisc-reconstituted TRPV2, which better approximates the physiological environment of the channel.
evidence: This is supported by the structural data from nanodisc-reconstituted samples

claim: The S4-S5 linker π-helix plays a critical role in ligand-dependent gating of TRPV2
source: confirms the critical role of the S4-S5 linker π-helix (S4-S5π-hinge) in ligand-dependent gating of TRPV2
evidence: This is supported by structural observations in the current study and previous work

claim: Classification of the TRPV2RTx-APOL sample revealed one C4 symmetric and two distinct C2 symmetric classes
source: Classification of the TRPV2RTx-APOL sample revealed the presence of four classes: one low-resolution (~7 Å) class, which was excluded from further analysis, and three higher resolution classes which are representative of three different conformations. These include one C4 symmetric and two distinct C2 symmetric classes refined to 2.9 Å, 3.3 Å and 4.2 Å, respectively (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly supported by the 3D classification results shown in Figure 1 and supplement

claim: 3D classification of the TRPV2RTx-ND converged on a single C2 symmetric conformation resolved to 3.8 Å
source: By contrast, 3D classification of the TRPV2RTx-ND converged on a single C2 symmetric conformation resolved to 3.8 Å (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 2–3).
evidence: This is directly supported by the 3D classification results

claim: The transmembrane domains of TRPV2RTx-APOL 1-3 show similarity to the apo form and adopt non-conducting conformations
source: Unexpectedly, the transmembrane domains (TM) of the three structures obtained from amphipol-reconstituted TRPV2, TRPV2RTx-APOL 1-3, show similarity to our previously solved cryo-EM structure of TRPV2 in its apo form (Zubcevic et al., 2016) (TRPV2APO) and adopt non-conducting conformations (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and HOLE profile analysis

claim: The TM domains of TRPV2RTx-APOL 1 and TRPV2RTx-APOL 2 structures largely retain C4 symmetry
source: While fully bound to RTx, the TM domains of TRPV2RTx-APOL 1 and TRPV2RTx-APOL 2 structures largely retain C4 symmetry (Figure 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in the figures

claim: The TMs of TRPV2RTx-APOL 3 exhibit a slight departure from C4 symmetry in the pore
source: However, the TMs of TRPV2RTx-APOL 3 exhibit a slight departure from C4 symmetry in the pore (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis

claim: RTx binding induces a 5° clockwise rotation of the ARD when viewed from the extracellular space
source: However, RTx binding induces a 5° clockwise rotation of the ARD when viewed from the extracellular space and a ~ 10 Å lateral widening of the cytoplasmic assembly (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison between TRPV2RTx-APOL 1 and TRPV2APO

claim: RTx causes a conformational change in the S4-S5 linker
source: In addition, RTx causes a conformational change in the S4-S5 linker (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), as well as a displacement of the TRP domain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison

claim: A π-helical turn is introduced at the junction of the S4-S5 linker and the S5 helix in the TRPV2RTx-APOL 1 structure, which is absent in TRPV2APO
source: The conformational change in the S4-S5 linker is caused by the introduction of a π-helical turn at the junction of the S4-S5 linker and the S5 helix in the TRPV2RTx-APOL 1 structure (S4-S5π-hinge), which is absent in TRPV2APO (Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis and electron density maps

claim: Amphipol constricts the TM and prevents conformational changes at the S4-S5 linker and the ARD from propagating to the TM domain
source: Instead, RTx only effects changes in its immediate binding site above the S4-S5 linker and in the parts of the channel not bound by amphipol, strongly suggesting that the polymer constricts the TM and prevents conformational changes at the S4-S5 linker and the ARD from propagating to the TM domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that TM domains remain closed despite RTx binding

claim: Metal ions are not visualized in the pores of any of the TRPV2RTx-APOL structures
source: Interestingly, metal ions are not visualized in the pores of any of the TRPV2RTx-APOL structures, despite the high resolutions obtained in this study.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM density maps

claim: Metal ions occupying the SF and the pores of thermoTRPV channels have only been captured in structures obtained by X-ray crystallography
source: Whether this is the result of cryo-EM experimental conditions is unclear, but thus far metal ions occupying the SF and the pores of thermoTRPV channels have only been captured in structures obtained by X-ray crystallography (Zubcevic et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is based on comparison with previous crystallographic studies

claim: RTx binding induces C2 symmetry in the nanodisc-reconstituted TRPV2 which extends throughout the channel
source: In stark contrast to the amphipol-reconstituted channel, RTx binding induces C2 symmetry in the nanodisc-reconstituted TRPV2 which extends throughout the channel.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis of TRPV2RTx-ND

claim: The symmetry of the TRPV2RTx-ND map yielded a CC = 0.9 and score of 1.28 for C2 symmetry
source: The symmetry of the TRPV2RTx-ND map was assessed both visually, and by the Map Symmetry function in Phenix which yielded a CC = 0.9 and score of 1.28 for C2 symmetry.
evidence: This is a quantitative assessment using computational tools

claim: C4 symmetry yielded a lower correlation coefficient (CC = 0.8) for TRPV2RTx-ND
source: For comparison, C4 symmetry yielded a lower correlation coefficient (CC = 0.8).
evidence: This is a quantitative assessment supporting C2 over C4 symmetry

claim: The pore of TRPV2RTx-ND adopts a C2 symmetric arrangement
source: The pore of TRPV2RTx-ND adopts a C2 symmetric arrangement (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is directly shown in Figure 2A

claim: The narrowest constriction between SF residues in diametrically opposing subunits A and C is ~11 Å in TRPV2RTx-ND
source: This arrangement creates a large C2 symmetric opening where the narrowest constriction between SF residues in diametrically opposing subunits A and C and B and D is ~11 Å and ~8 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is a measurement from the structure shown in Figure 2

claim: The narrowest constriction between SF residues in diametrically opposing subunits B and D is ~8 Å in TRPV2RTx-ND
source: This arrangement creates a large C2 symmetric opening where the narrowest constriction between SF residues in diametrically opposing subunits A and C and B and D is ~11 Å and ~8 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is a measurement from the structure shown in Figure 2

claim: The SF of TRPV2RTx-ND has ample room to accommodate large organic cations
source: This results in an SF with ample room to accommodate large organic cations (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is inferred from the measured dimensions of the SF opening

claim: The pore helix of subunit A swivels by ~10° in TRPV2RTx-ND
source: A closer look at the pore helices reveals that this arrangement in the SF is achieved through a ~ 10° swivel of the subunit A pore helix, which brings the N-terminal part of the helix closer to S5 while distancing it from S6 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is measured from the structure shown in Figure 2C

claim: The position of the pore helices controls the size and the shape of the SF in TRPV2
source: The position of the pore helices controls the size and the shape of the SF, and appears to exert control over ion permeation in TRPV2.
evidence: This is inferred from structural observations and comparison of different states

claim: In TRPV2RTx-ND, the S6 helix of subunits A and C adopts a straight α-helical, closed conformation
source: In subunits A and C, the S6 helix adopts a straight α-helical, closed conformation, while the S6 of subunits B and D is bent and the common gate apparently open (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is observed in the structure shown in Figure 2A

claim: In TRPV2RTx-ND, the S6 of subunits B and D is bent and the common gate apparently open
source: In subunits A and C, the S6 helix adopts a straight α-helical, closed conformation, while the S6 of subunits B and D is bent and the common gate apparently open (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is observed in the structure shown in Figure 2A

claim: The overall functional state of the common gate in TRPV2RTx-ND is likely non-conductive
source: However, the overall functional state of the common gate is likely non-conductive as the gate residues from subunits A and C would presumably hinder ion permeation.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement where two subunits remain closed

claim: Rotation of subunits around the S4-S5π-hinge results in the distinct C2 symmetric arrangement observed in TRPV2RTx-ND
source: Similar to our previous findings, this alignment shows that the two subunits diverge at the S4-S5 linker and the PH and indicates that rotation of subunits around the S4-S5π-hinge appears to result in the distinct C2 symmetric arrangement observed in TRPV2RTx-ND (Figure 3—figure supplements 4–5).
evidence: This is inferred from structural alignment and comparison

claim: The TM domains of TRPV2RTx-ND contract in an asymmetric manner compared to TRPV2APO
source: When compared to the TRPV2APO, the TM domains of the TRPV2RTx-ND structure appear to contract in an asymmetric manner (Figure 3A), while the ARD assembly expands by ~10 Å and rotates by 3° (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison shown in Figure 3

claim: The ARD assembly expands by ~10 Å and rotates by 3° in TRPV2RTx-ND compared to TRPV2APO
source: When compared to the TRPV2APO, the TM domains of the TRPV2RTx-ND structure appear to contract in an asymmetric manner (Figure 3A), while the ARD assembly expands by ~10 Å and rotates by 3° (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is measured from structural comparison shown in Figure 3B

claim: RTx-binding to TRPV2 in lipid membranes induces a rigid-body rotation of the entire subunit that originates at the S4-S5π-hinge
source: This coupled movement of the TM and ARD indicates that RTx-binding to TRPV2 in lipid membranes induces a rigid-body rotation of the entire subunit that originates at the S4-S5π-hinge (Figure 3D–E).
evidence: This is inferred from the coupled movements observed in structural comparisons

claim: TRPV2RTx-ND exhibits different degrees of reduced symmetry from TRPV2RTx-XTAL
source: Interestingly, the TRPV2RTx-ND structure exhibits different degrees of reduced symmetry from the previously determined crystal structure of TRPV2 in complex with RTx (TRPV2RTx-XTAL) (Zubcevic et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison between the two structures

claim: The TM domains of TRPV2RTx-ND contract in a two-fold symmetric manner compared to TRPV2RTx-XTAL
source: Compared to the TRPV2RTx-XTAL, the TM domains of TRPV2RTx-ND contract in an two-fold symmetric manner (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison shown in Figure 4A

claim: The overall fold of TRPV2RTx-ND is closer to C4 symmetry than that of TRPV2RTx-XTAL
source: This conformational change, which stems from rotation of individual TRPV2RTx-ND subunits around the S4-S5π-hinge (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), results in an overall fold that is closer to C4 symmetry than that of the TRPV2RTx-XTAL (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison and measurements shown in Figure 4B

claim: The pore helices and the SF of TRPV2RTx-ND remain distinctly C2 symmetric
source: However, while the TRPV2RTx-ND helices S1-S6 adopt a more C4 symmetric arrangement, the pore helices and the SF remain distinctly C2 symmetric (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is observed from structural analysis shown in Figure 4C

claim: The SF of TRPV2RTx-ND is wider than that of TRPV2RTx-XTAL
source: Remarkably, the SF of TRPV2RTx-ND is wider than that of TRPV2RTx-XTAL, and the two structures display different C2 symmetric openings at the SF (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison shown in Figure 4C

claim: In TRPV2RTx-XTAL, a network of interactions between Y542-T602-Y627 in subunits A and C tethers the pore helices to S5 and S6
source: In the TRPV2RTx-XTAL structure, the pore helices of subunits B and D, which assume a widened conformation, are free of interactions with the pore domain, while a network of interactions (presumably hydrogen bonds) between Y542-T602-Y627 in subunits A and C tethers the pore helices to S5 and S6.
evidence: This is observed from the crystal structure

claim: Disruption of Y542-T602-Y627 interactions is detrimental to the permeation of large organic cations but has no effect on permeation of metal ions
source: Our previous work showed that disruption of these interactions is detrimental to the permeation of large organic cations but has no effect on permeation of metal ions (Zubcevic et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is based on previous functional studies by the authors

claim: The putative hydrogen bond triad is disrupted in all four subunits of the TRPV2RTx-ND structure
source: Interestingly, the putative hydrogen bond triad is disrupted in all four subunits of the TRPV2RTx-ND structure (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is observed from the structure shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: The putative hydrogen bond triad is an essential part of the transition between closed and open states of the channel
source: This suggests that the putative hydrogen bond triad, while not a feature of the fully open SF, is an essential part of the transition between closed and open states of the channel.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the triad is present in intermediate states but not in the fully open state

claim: Extensive rearrangements around the SF and the PH during gating have only been observed in TRPV1 and TRPV2 channels
source: It is interesting to point out that extensive rearrangements around the SF and the PH during gating have thus far only been observed in structural studies of TRPV1 (Cao et al., 2013b) and TRPV2 (Zubcevic et al., 2018a) channels.
evidence: This is based on comparison with structures of other TRPV subfamily members

claim: In the non-conductive state, the SFs of TRPV3-TRPV6 adopt a conformation that is wide enough to accommodate a semi-hydrated cation
source: In the non-conductive state, the SFs of the remaining members of the TRPV subfamily (TRPV3-TRPV6 [Zubcevic et al., 2018b; Singh et al., 2018; Deng et al., 2018; Hughes et al., 2018; McGoldrick et al., 2018]) adopt a conformation that is wide enough to accommodate a semi-hydrated cation, and do not move appreciably during channel activation.
evidence: This is based on structural studies of other TRPV channels cited

claim: TRPV1 and TRPV2 are the only members of the TRPV subfamily that possess a gate at the SF
source: This may indicate that TRPV1 and TRPV2 are the only members of the TRPV subfamily that possess a gate at the SF, and that the coupling of structural elements necessary for activation of these channels differs from that of TRPV3-TRPV6 (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of gating mechanisms across TRPV subfamily members

claim: RTx assumes different binding poses in subunits of the C2-symmetric structures in both amphipol and nanodisc samples
source: As observed in our previous study (Zubcevic et al., 2018a), RTx assumes different binding poses in subunits of the C2-symmetric structures, both in the amphipol and the nanodisc samples (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) which may lead to the distinct conformations observed in these channels.
evidence: This is observed from the structures shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3

claim: The pore turret occupies the space within the membrane plane between S5 and the VSLD in rat TRPV2
source: Interestingly, a recent structure of rat TRPV2 with the pore turret resolved showed that this region, which contains a large number of charged and polar residues, occupies the space within the membrane plane between S5 and the Voltage Sensor-Like Domain (VSLD) (Dosey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on a recent structure of rat TRPV2

claim: The pore turret is the least conserved region amongst the TRPV2 orthologs
source: Indeed, the pore turret is the least conserved region amongst the TRPV2 orthologs, and the variations in its sequence might indicate that the turret adopts different conformations in TRPV2 channels from different species.
evidence: This is inferred from sequence comparison and structural observations

claim: The omission of the pore turret from the construct used in the crystallographic study is not the cause of the C2 symmetry
source: Nevertheless, our study clearly shows that the omission of this region from the construct used in the crystallographic study of the TRPV2/RTx complex is not the cause of the C2 symmetry.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that full-length TRPV2 also shows C2 symmetry

claim: TRPV2RTx-XTAL precedes TRPV2RTx-ND in the conformational activation trajectory
source: We propose that TRPV2RTx-XTAL precedes TRPV2RTx-ND in the conformational activation trajectory based on two observations.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on structural and functional considerations

claim: The common gate is fully closed in TRPV2RTx-XTAL
source: Firstly, the common gate is fully closed in the TRPV2RTx-XTAL while it adopts an apparently partially open conformation in TRPV2RTx-ND (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5

claim: The putative hydrogen bond network between S5 and S6 and the pore helix is essential for the channel's ability to transition to a fully open SF that can accommodate large organic cations
source: Secondly, our previous studies have shown that the putative hydrogen bond network between S5 and S6 and the pore helix is essential for the channel's ability to transition to a fully open SF that can accommodate large organic cations (Zubcevic et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is based on previous functional studies

claim: RTx induces C2 symmetric conformations of TRPV2 in both amphipol and nanodiscs, negating the hypothetical role of crystallization artefacts
source: Here, we have conducted a study that reveals symmetry transitions associated with gating of the TRPV2 channel by RTx. Interestingly, our data shows that RTx induces C2 symmetric conformations of TRPV2 in both amphipol and nanodiscs, and it thereby negates the hypothetical role of crystallization artefacts and crystal packing bias in stabilising two-fold symmetry.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation of C2 symmetry in multiple environments

claim: C2 symmetry in TRPV2 is independent of the presence or absence of the pore turret region
source: Similarly, C2 symmetry in TRPV2 is independent of the presence or absence of the pore turret region, suggesting that this region does not play an essential role in the regulation of the SF in rabbit TRPV2.
evidence: This is concluded from comparison of structures with and without the pore turret

claim: Amphipols constrict the TM domains and stabilize low-energy pre-open states
source: These data, while adding valuable data points to the conformational landscape of TRPV2, also illustrate the potential caveats of using amphipols in studies of conformational changes in the transmembrane domains of proteins, as they appear to constrict the TM domains and stabilize low-energy pre-open states (Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that TM domains remain closed in amphipol

claim: The TRPV2RTx-ND dataset yielded a single, two-fold symmetric structure
source: The TRPV2RTx-ND dataset yielded a single, two-fold symmetric structure thus giving strong evidence that RTx stabilizes two-fold symmetric conformational states in the TRPV2 channel in lipid membranes.
evidence: This is directly observed from the data processing results

claim: In TRPV2RTx-ND, the common gate adopts an intermediate conformation where the gate is apparently open in one set of diagonally opposing subunits and closed in the other
source: However, in nanodiscs TRPV2 is captured with its SF fully open and its common gate in an intermediate conformation where the gate is apparently open in one set of diagonally opposing subunits and closed in the other.
evidence: This is observed from the structure of TRPV2RTx-ND

claim: TRPV2, as it travels toward the final open state, would adopt further conformations that increasingly approximate C4 symmetry
source: Therefore, it is possible that TRPV2, as it travels toward the final open state where both the SF and the common gate are fully open, would adopt further conformations that increasingly approximate C4 symmetry (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the observed trend

claim: The symmetry of the SF does not appear to be dictated by the symmetry of the overall channel
source: Because the symmetry of the SF does not appear to be dictated by the symmetry of the overall channel, we cannot exclude the possibility that the final open state might indeed possess a C2 symmetric SF while otherwise adopting a nearly C4 symmetric conformation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that SF symmetry differs from overall channel symmetry

claim: C2 symmetric states play a role in the permeation of large organic cations in TRPV2
source: Our previous functional studies have suggested that C2 symmetric states play a role in the permeation of large organic cations and consequently in the full opening of the SF (Zubcevic et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is based on previous functional studies

claim: The channel might be utilizing C2 symmetric states as means to achieve full opening in a step-wise manner
source: Hence, the channel might be utilizing C2 symmetric states as means to achieve full opening in a step-wise manner.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the observed intermediate states

claim: C2 symmetric states elicited by ligand binding have been observed in TRPV3 and TRPM2 channels
source: Similar C2 symmetric states elicited by ligand binding have been observed in TRPV3 (Zubcevic et al., 2018b) and TRPM2 (Yin et al., 2018) channels, which opens up the possibility that C2 symmetry might be widely associated with gating in members of the TRP channel superfamily.
evidence: This is based on structural studies of other TRP channels

claim: The human BK channel also enters C2 symmetric states
source: Intriguingly, a recent cryo-EM study of the human BK channel reconstituted in liposomes showed that this channel also enters C2 symmetric states (Tonggu and Wang, 2018), suggesting that two-fold symmetry might also play a role in the molecular mechanisms of other tetrameric ion channels.
evidence: This is based on a recent cryo-EM study of BK channel

claim: The arrangement of pore helices in TRPV2RTx-ND resembles that observed in TPC and NaV
source: Interestingly, the arrangement of pore helices in TRPV2RTx-ND resembles that observed in TPC and NaV (Figure 6) and the selectivity filters in all three channels form a 'coin-slot' (Hille, 1971) opening.
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison shown in Figure 6

claim: The selectivity filters of TPC and NaV remain static during channel gating to maintain the structure necessary for Na+ selectivity
source: However, while the selectivity filters of TPC and NaV remain static during channel gating in order to maintain the structure necessary for Na+ selectivity, the SF of TRPV2 displays a large degree of plasticity.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of TPC and NaV gating mechanisms and comparison with TRPV2

claim: The two-fold symmetry observed in TRPV2 arises in response to conformational changes in the TM domains induced by ligand binding
source: Moreover, the two-fold symmetry observed in TRPV2 is unique in that it arises in response to conformational changes in the TM domains induced by ligand binding.
evidence: This is concluded from the structural observations in this study

claim: The two-fold symmetry in TPC and NaV stems from the arrangement of their respective homologous tandem repeats
source: By contrast, the two-fold symmetry in TPC and NaV stems from the arrangement of their respective homologous tandem repeats.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of TPC and NaV structure

claim: The construct for RTx sensitive, full-length rabbit TRPV2 was prepared by introducing four point mutations (F470S, L505M, L508T and Q528E) into the synthesized full-length rabbit TRPV2 gene
source: The construct for the RTx sensitive, full-length rabbit TRPV2 (TRPV2RTx) was prepared by introducing four point mutations (F470S, L505M, L508T and Q528E) into the synthesized full-length rabbit TRPV2 gene (Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used to prepare the construct

claim: The protein was expressed by infecting Sf9 cells with baculovirus at a density of 1.3 M cells ml−1 and incubating at 27°C for 72 hr
source: The protein was expressed by infecting Sf9 cells with baculovirus at a density of 1.3 M cells ml−1 and incubating at 27oC for 72 hr in an orbital shaker.
evidence: This describes the experimental method for protein expression

claim: Data for both TRPV2RTx-APOL and TRPV2RTx-ND were collected using the Titan Krios transmission electron microscope operating at 300 keV
source: Data for both TRPV2RTx-APOL and TRPV2RTx-ND were collected using the Titan Krios transmission electron microscope (TEM) operating at 300 keV using a Falcon III Direct Electron Detector operating in counting mode at a nominal magnification of 75,000x corresponding to a physical pixel size of 1.08 Å/pixel.
evidence: This describes the experimental method for data collection

claim: For TRPV2RTx-APOL, 1293 movies were collected with a total exposure of 42 e-/Å²
source: For the TRPV2RTx-APOL 1293 movies (30 frames/movie) were collected using a 60 s exposure with an exposure rate of ~0.8 e-/pixel/s, resulting in a total exposure of 42 e-/Å (Cao et al., 2013a) and a nominal defocus range from −1.25 µm to −3.0 µm.
evidence: This describes the experimental parameters for data collection

claim: For TRPV2RTx-ND, 2254 movies were collected with a total exposure of 42 e-/Å²
source: For TRPV2RTx-ND, 2254 movies were collected (30 frames/movie) with 60 s exposure and exposure rate of ~0.8 e-/pixel/s. The total exposure was of 42 e-/Å (Cao et al., 2013a) and a nominal defocus range from −1.25 µm to −3.0 µm.
evidence: This describes the experimental parameters for data collection
